title: FlyWire wiring predicts neuropil calcium correlations beyond distance in 50 flies; walking and rest coupling agree after global-signal removal; transmitter-matched wiring adds no gain
abstract: Question: does whole-brain wiring predict region-to-region functional connectivity (FC) in behaving Drosophila, does this coupling change between rest and walking, and does wiring from the matched transmitter class predict the FC of class-specific imaging lines better? Data: light-field calcium imaging of 75 brain regions (Aimon et al. 2023; 82 experiments; pan-neuronal, Cha, Gad, Vglut, TH, Trh and TDC lines) and the FlyWire v783 connectome (139,255 proofread neurons). Structural connectivity (SC) was the symmetric log synaptic flow between regions. We controlled for distance between region centroids and used flies as units. Results: group FC (50 flies) correlated with SC at Spearman rho = 0.48; distance-partial rho = 0.37, above a distance-stratified null (0.24 +/- 0.01; p < 0.0002). Distance alone explained R2 = 0.55 of group FC and SC added 0.06. In single flies the distance-partial coupling was 0.18 (95% CI 0.14-0.21) and positive in 48 of 50 flies; the between-fly FC agreement was rho = 0.58. Walking raised mean FC. Raw coupling was lower in walking by 0.013 to 0.036 in rho (clear only in the 20 flies with at least 60 s per state, p = 0.004). After global-signal regression the walk-rest difference was within +/-0.025 in all three state definitions (Wilcoxon p = 0.19 to 0.92). The walk-related FC change did not repeat between flies and did not follow SC. Coupling was highest in optic lobe, AMMC, SAD, IPS and GNG and lowest in the central complex and antennal lobe (split-half reliability rho = 0.86). Transmitter-matched SC gave no specific gain (permutation p = 0.37-0.66). Limitations: light-field blur can mix adjacent regions and distance control cannot remove all of it; connectome and activity come from different flies; states come from a convolved walk regressor; class SC matrices are highly correlated, so the class test has low power.
